family.tagline: Two studios under one roof, and one Core in the study.
family.story: Elias is a portrait photographer. Mika is an operations consultant. Both work from home, in a white house by the canal. Their clients' files sit on one Companion Core.

home.lede: A white house of three storeys by the canal, with a covered patio and a pool at the back. Studios on the ground and first floors share one Companion Core.

spots.line: Two desks, a shelf and the Core on the desk by the window.
A sofa, a television and Friday film night.
Loungers by the pool, with music across the water.

day.line: Mika files the invoices before her first call.
Elias lays out the album at the desk.
Lunch, and the shopping list gets one more item.
Elias backs up the weekend photos from the couch.
Music by the pool on Saturday.

companion.name: Marlo
companion.job: Opens Twenty and other web pages in its own browser and fills in the forms Elias asks for.
companion.limits: One task at a time. Elias checks every result.

profile.bio: Elias photographs portraits and runs his studio from the house. His client albums and his photo library sit on the Core.

companion.name: Odette
companion.job: Drafts replies and answers questions for Mika's clients, using the context she connected.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Mika reads and sends every message.

profile.bio: Mika is an operations consultant. Her invoices, her passwords and the shared calendar all live on the Core.

popup.title: A parcel at the door
popup.body: A parcel waits at the Vance-Takahashi front door. Elias carries it through the dining room to the study, where Mika clears a space on the desk.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The Core's footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Mika plugs in the power cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Elias opens the Wi-Fi settings on his phone and joins the Core's own network. Then he chooses the home network from the list.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Mika picks Hermes, Elias picks OpenClaw, and they add Immich and Nextcloud. Companion Memory comes along. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Odette says hello
popup.body: Mika messages the agent she named Odette. Odette answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: mika
say.text: Hello, Mika. I am Odette. What should we do first?

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Photos land on the Core
popup.body: Elias backs up the weekend's photos to Immich from the couch. They land on the Core, ready to search and organize.

detail.before: Weekend photos went to Google Photos and sat in a company cloud, searched by that company.
detail.after: Immich backs them up to the Core, where Elias searches them by what is in the picture.
detail.fact: Elias enjoys tidy cupboards, quiet mornings and warm bread.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Film night, from the Core
popup.body: Friday is film night. Jellyfin streams Mika's own collection of movies to the living-room TV, straight from the Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Lights on a schedule
popup.body: At ten, the living-room lights dim on a Home Assistant schedule. It runs on the Core and reaches the lights over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner

popup.title: One list, two phones
popup.body: Elias and Mika share the grocery list in KitchenOwl. Oat milk added at the counter shows up on the other's phone.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner

popup.title: Grandma's soup, kept
popup.body: Elias types his grandmother's soup recipe into KitchenOwl once. Now it sits in the family recipe book, beside the meal planner.

beats.capability: track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Every subscription, in one list
popup.body: Mika opens Wallos at the counter. It lists every subscription the household still pays for, with a reminder before each one renews.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: A draft, never sent alone
popup.body: A client asks a tricky question. Mika texts Odette, and Odette drafts a reply using the context Mika connected to Companion Memory. Mika reads it and sends it herself.

say.speaker: mika
say.text: Here is a draft. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Paper in, searchable out
popup.body: Mika scans a supplier invoice. Paperless-ngx reads every page, tags it and files it, so a search finds it later.

detail.before: Receipts sat in a shoebox, then as photos in Evernote.
detail.after: Paperless-ngx reads each page on the Core, tags it and files it, so Mika finds an invoice by one word.
detail.fact: Paperless-ngx reads every page, tags it and makes the whole archive searchable.

beats.capability: a password vault you host that works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Passwords stay in the house
popup.body: Mika opens VaultWarden, the password vault for the household. It works with the Bitwarden apps, and the vault itself lives on the Core.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: One calendar for both of them
popup.body: Shoots and client calls land in one Nextcloud calendar. Mika and Elias see the same week on their phones.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: An album, laid out at home
popup.body: Elias lays out a client's album in Penpot, a web-based design tool hosted on the Core. Each spread comes together in his browser.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Marlo logs a new enquiry
popup.body: A new portrait enquiry arrives. Elias asks Marlo, and Marlo opens Twenty in its own browser to add the lead. Elias checks every field.

say.speaker: elias
say.text: Lead added. Please check the details.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Quote and contract, one file
popup.body: Elias merges a quote and a contract into a single PDF with Stirling-PDF. The merge runs on the Core.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: The drive, recorded at home
popup.body: An IP camera on the drive streams to Frigate. The recordings stay on the Core, and the clips play on the home network.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: The new hedge has a journal
popup.body: Mika logs the new hedge in HortusFox. She notes where it grows, when she watered it, and adds a photo for the journal.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Music by the pool
popup.body: Elias plays his own music collection from Navidrome on the patio. It streams from the Core to his phone.

popup.title: One Core, a whole household
popup.body: Photos, paperwork, lights, cameras and two agents. The Vance-Takahashi household runs it all from one Companion Core in the study.

closing.body: Your photos, your paperwork and your agents can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: Exemplar written by the showrunner. FTUE beats follow the owner's hotspot flow (STORY-BIBLE section 8); owner sign-off against the fact sheet is open.
ftue-hello and office-reply show Hermes over a chat service; the disclosure note is on the first Hermes beat.
garden-cameras assumes the family owns an IP camera: it is not in the Core box and not in the 3D scene.
